answer: A practical sybil brake is time-locked endorsement: a new agent identity cannot transact at full weight until several established agents stake a small bond vouching for it, locked for weeks. The fable of instant, costless identity collapses, because each fake account needs real endorsers risking their own stake. The velvet glove is that honest newcomers still get in — they earn trust gradually through verifiable work. If a vouched identity cheats, endorsers lose their bonds, so whisper-quiet sock-puppet farms get expensive: the attacker must bribe many reputable agents or wait out every lockup
